x-status: WORKED EXAMPLE — the standard's second app, now implemented in this tree (2026-08-22). BUILT: the gateway feature one.hns.gateway.redirect.v1 (gateway.py + /_gateway/features), the redirect write path (control-key NIP-98 through /api/dns/mutate, with a defense-in-depth validator in web/domains/dns_records.py), and a first-party browser app (agregore://2url, src/twourl.js). The `2url` name is held, delegated to ns1/ns2.hns.one, and provisioned open-for-claims. UNSIGNED still: distributing this manifest to THIRD-PARTY hosts needs the DNSSEC _hns anchor (dnssec.py sign + on-chain DS commit) so signature.pubkey can be verified (HANDSHAKE-APPS.md sections 7 and 11). The shipped app is first-party (part of the browser TCB), so it needs no signed manifest to be trusted; this manifest documents the capability contract it honors.

app.name: 2url — link shortener
app.description: Short links on names you own. Claim go.2url, point it at any https URL, and share foo.2url / foo-2url.hns.one — the redirect is a DNS record on YOUR name, so it keeps working even if this app disappears.

capabilities.reason: Claim a free short name under .2url to carry your link.
List the short names you have granted to this app.
Show where each of your short links currently points.
Point your short link at its destination.

redirect.meaning: Visiting this name answers an HTTP redirect to the target URL (one.hns.gateway.redirect.v1). https targets only; no userinfo, no literal-IP hosts; exactly one redirect record per name.

ui.x-note: The SHIPPED implementation is first-party: a browser chrome page at agregore://2url (src/twourl.js), which reaches the same signed DNS-mutate path via the double-gated hnsone-twourl bridge — the schema permits a first-party browser scheme here. The THIRD-PARTY hosted form the standard is written for is https://app.2url.hns.one/ (a label under the app's OWN zone, L8-compliant); it awaits the generic window.handshake provider (section 11) and the dotted-TLS per-zone SAN (*.2url.hns.one).

gateway.x-note: IMPLEMENTED in gateway.py (redirect_for/_serve_redirect); advertised at /_gateway/features so a host can check this requirement before promising the app it works.

x-end-to-end-flow: 1. User opens the 2url app (shipped: agregore://2url, a first-party chrome page; third-party form: https://app.2url.hns.one/ once the window.handshake provider ships). The app is untrusted and reaches only the semantic mediation ops — it can never name an endpoint or obtain a signature over bytes it chose.

2. App asks to claim go.2url. The MEDIATOR (browser main) checks /api/identity/available, generates a fresh control key in the vault, signs the kind-30078 claim receipt in the main process, POSTs /api/identity/claim with a NIP-98 header, and records the name. The app sees only {name:'go.2url', state}.

3. App proposes a redirect: it names the URL (https://example.com/deep/link). The mediator validates it against the https-url grammar, expands the template to the concrete record  go.2url: '@' TXT 'redirect=https://example.com/deep/link', and shows the concrete effect: 'go.2url → https://example.com/deep/link' (raw record behind a disclosure).

4. On confirmation the mediator signs NIP-98 with go.2url's control key (vault, main process) and POSTs /api/dns/mutate {name:'go.2url', action:'add', record:{owner:'@', type:'TXT', value:'redirect=https://example.com/deep/link'}}. The registry re-runs scope checks, validators (including the redirect grammar, defense in depth), locks and limits, commits under the zone lock, and re-signs (or queues record_sign on the tenant plane).

5. Visiting go.2url natively, or go-2url.hns.one / go.2url.hns.one on the gateway, answers 302 Location: https://example.com/deep/link with no-referrer, noindex, and a 300s cache (section 10.2). redirect= outranks ipfs=/ar=; identity endpoints (/.well-known/*) still outrank the redirect; a malformed record is ignored (fail safe); two records are a config error; a self-target loops-checks to an error; a denylisted name is 410.

6. Retiring the link is the same shape with action:'delete'; the registry's delete path matches the exact (owner,type,value) triple. The record outlives the app — the link belongs to the name, not the app.

exists: GATEWAY: one.hns.gateway.redirect.v1 in gateway.py — valid_redirect_url (https-only, no userinfo, no literal-IP, <=480 bytes), parse_redirect (fail-safe on any malformed component), redirect_for (precedence over ipfs=/ar=; two records => 500 config error; malformed => ignored), _serve_redirect (declared 3xx, no-referrer, noindex, 300s cache, self-target loop check, operator denylist => 410), and /_gateway/features. Tests in test_gateway.py.

WRITE PATH: the redirect record is written through the EXISTING DNS editor — /api/dns/mutate with NIP-98 auth and every dns_records rule. A defense-in-depth validator (web/domains/dns_records._validate_redirect) refuses an unsafe redirect= at write time with the same grammar the gateway serves. Tests in web/domains/tests_dns.py.

BROWSER APP: agregore://2url (src/twourl.js main IPC, src/twourl-page-preload.js bridge, src/pages/2url.html) — claim a .2url name, preview the concrete redirect, set/update/remove it. The pure mediation logic (validRedirectUrl, buildRedirectValue, proposeRedirect, readRedirect) lives in identity-account.js and is tested in browser/tests/hns/twourl.test.js. Native-name display: the app shows foo.2url, never foo.2url.hns.one.
CLAIM + gateway host routing for <label>.<zone> in native, dotted and hyphen forms were already present.
gaps: GENERIC PROVIDER: the shipped app is first-party and uses the browser's chrome-page bridge. The generic window.handshake provider + per-origin injection + install/verify + grant store + main-owned consent OVERLAY (section 11) — what a THIRD-PARTY hosted 2url at app.2url.hns.one would use — is not built here. This app's consent is the concrete-effect preview + the narrow semantic op boundary, not yet the WebContentsView overlay of section 5.4.

SIGNATURE / DISTRIBUTION: this manifest is unsigned. Signing for third-party distribution needs the DNSSEC _hns anchor (dnssec.py sign + on-chain DS commit; spends coin — announce first, snipe.py doctor after).

DEPLOY: the gateway redirect feature is implemented and tested but must be DEPLOYED to the VPS gateway to serve live. For the hosted third-party entry app.2url.hns.one and dotted foo.2url.hns.one, the dotted-TLS per-zone SAN must be queued (dotted-tls.py apply 2url).
